comments.author: dnautics
comments.story_title: Ask HN: Resources to encourage teen on becoming computer engineer?
comments.why_zh: 无论职业方向如何，基础的硬件知识都很有价值。
comments.quote_zh: 那套从零开始搭一台计算机的视频系列非常棒。
comments.text_zh: 1）那套从零开始搭一台计算机的视频系列非常棒。无论你最终处在技术栈的哪一层（甚至如果你最后不从事技术行业），这些信息都很有价值；而且深入了解这些系统在以后会相当有价值，因为我们现在已经不太教孩子们硬件方面的东西了。[VIDEO] 2）如果他们的兴趣在技术栈更靠上的位置（比如机器人），而且不介意钻进细节里、在社区里求助，我会建议以 raspberry pi 系统为学习目标。我更偏好的目标是 Nerves；它更精简一些，也不是所有东西都有驱动，但社区非常棒（elixir 的 slack / nerves 就是该待的地方），而且很容易就能做到把你丢进一个 IDE 里，直接开始写代码。
comments.text: 1) the video series on building an computer from scratch is fantastic. It's valuable information no matter where in the tech stack you wind up in (or even if you don't wind up in tech) but also having a deep knowledge of these systems will be of considerable value down the line, because we aren't training kids in hardware as much anymore. [VIDEO] 2) If their interest is a bit higher in the stack (like robotics e.g.), and they don't mind getting in the weeds and asking for help in the community, I would target learning with a raspberry pi system. My preferred target is Nerves; it's a bit more bare-bones, and there aren't drivers for everything, but the community is fantastic (the elixir slack / nerves is the place to be), and it's easy to get to a point where you are dropped into an IDE and you can just code .

comments.author: ruslan
comments.story_title: What Happens When a CPU Starts
comments.why_zh: 既长知识又有趣的面包板 6502 计算机搭建。
comments.quote_zh: 我觉得 Ben Eater 那套用 6502 CPU 搭建简易 8 位面包板计算机的系列既长知识又有趣。
comments.text_zh: MOS6502 的启动过程并不像文章说的那么简单。它会花大约 7 个时钟周期做内部初始化，然后才从复位向量（0xFFFC/0xFFFD）取出第一条跳转指令的地址。我觉得 Ben Eater 那套用 6502 CPU 搭建简易 8 位面包板计算机的系列既长知识又有趣。[VIDEO]
comments.text: Starting procedure on MOS6502 is not that simple as it is told in the article. It spends some 7 clocks on doing internal initialization and only then fetches address of first jump from reset vector (0xFFFC/0xFFFD). I find Ben's Eater series on building simple 8-bit breadboard computer using 6502 CPU very educating and entertaining. [VIDEO]

comments.author: zurkog
comments.why_zh: Ben Eater 的系列搭建的是 Malvino 的 SAP 计算机。
comments.quote_zh: Ben Eater 做这些视频做得非常出色，把每个概念都讲清楚了
comments.text_zh: 这本书太酷了。Ben Eater 做这些视频做得非常出色，把每个概念都讲清楚了，不过他搭建的那台计算机（SAP，即 Simple As Possible）直接来自 Albert Paul Malvino 1977 年的《Digital Computer Electronics》。他甚至在第一期视频里提到这本书，还展示了一本：[VIDEO] 我 4 年前照着这个 instructable 做的时候偶然发现了这本书：[LINK] 那个 instructable 远没有 Ben 的视频细致，但当时那是我唯一的资料，而且它推荐了这本书。注意：我 4 年前买这本书时只要 5 美元，现在我看到它卖到 99 美元以上：[LINK] 平装版只要 22 美元，但它的作者名单里多了一位 1977 年版没有的作者，所以我不知道它是不是完全同一本书。
comments.text: This was so cool as a book. Ben Eater did a fantastic job of making these videos, explaining each concept, but the computer he builds (the SAP, or Simple As Possible) is directly from "Digital Computer Electronics" (c) 1977 by Albert Paul Malvino. He even goes so far as to mention it and shows a copy of the book in his first video: [VIDEO] I stumbled across the book 4 years ago when I followed this instructable: [LINK] The instructable is nowhere near as detailed as Ben's videos, but it was all I had at the time, and it recommended that book. Note: when I purchased the book 4 years ago, it was only $5, now I'm seeing it for upwards of $99: [LINK] The paperback is only $22, but it lists an additional author not present on the 1977 version, so I don't know if it's the exact same book.
